subject.title: fix(agents): xAI/Grok requests fail after a stale reasoning replay ("could not decrypt encrypted_content")

question: Should maintainers accept source-level predicate coverage plus redacted pre-fix production logs as sufficient proof for this provider-side xAI stale encrypted_content retry fix, or keep requiring after-fix real Grok/gateway output before merge?
rationale: The normal external-PR gate requires after-fix real behavior proof, but the author plausibly explains that the exact code-less xAI decrypt error depends on provider-owned snapshot/key rotation and cannot be induced on demand without testing a different error path.

options.title: Accept a proof override
options.body: Treat the pre-fix production logs, dependency-backed SDK error shape, and positive/negative unit tests as sufficient for this narrow matcher and proceed after ordinary branch refresh and CI gates.

options.title: Require organic after-fix proof
options.body: Keep the PR blocked until a future redacted Grok/gateway log shows the fixed retry path during an organic xAI rotation event.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Leave the linked issue open but pause this branch if maintainers want broader provider error-classification design before accepting another predicate match.

recommendation.title: Accept a proof override
recommendation.body: Treat the pre-fix production logs, dependency-backed SDK error shape, and positive/negative unit tests as sufficient for this narrow matcher and proceed after ordinary branch refresh and CI gates.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the closest merged recovery precedent in the same predicate and explicitly documented a similar provider-generated stale-reasoning proof limitation in PR 92941.
